rem:q-exp-p-adic: Remark p-adic realisations of \exp_q (\mathbb{Q}_p and \mathbb{C}_p). The truncated \mathbb{F}_p-exponential lifts to a convergent grouplike on \mathbb{Q}_p and \mathbb{C}_p when q is p-adically close to 1. For q \in 1 + p\mathbb{Z}_p, the Jackson factorial satisfies v_p([n]_q!) = v_p(n!). Over \mathbb{C}_p, the series converges for v_p(x) > 1/(p - 1), exactly matching the classical p-adic exponential radius.

def:q-logarithm:
Definition q-Logarithm (categorical adjoint). A primitive of \mathcal{H}_q satisfies \Delta_q(p) = p \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes p and \epsilon(p) = 0. The q-logarithm is the unique primitive \log_q \in \mathrm{Prim}(\mathcal{H}_q) satisfying

  \log_q \circ \exp_q \;=\; \mathrm{id}.
rem:q-logarithm-remark: Remark The q-logarithm as an adjoint. The q-logarithm acts as the left adjoint of the grouplike-of functor from primitives to grouplikes.
rem:q-logarithm-properties: Remark Realisations of \log_q: base ring, three contexts, Habiro ring, and Reeb-flow rapidity. The q-logarithm is base-ring independent. The adjoint pair (\log_q, \exp_q) operates on the formal-power-series ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}[\![x]\!] over the Habiro ring. It measures the cosmological displacement in Hopf-algebraic units as the infinitesimal generator of the Reeb-flow holonomy.
prop:q-logarithm-exists: Proposition Existence of the q-logarithm primitive. Under the hypotheses securing \exp_q, there exists a unique primitive \log_q \in \mathrm{Prim}(\mathcal{H}_q) satisfying \log_q \circ \exp_q = \mathrm{id}.
prf:q-logarithm-exists:
Proof Proof of existence of the q-logarithm primitive. By Milnor--Moore, \mathrm{Prim}(\mathcal{H}_q) is the Lie algebra of the grouplike group G(\mathcal{H}_q), so the formal inverse of \exp_q exists as a primitive whenever \exp_q is bijective onto its image. Explicitly, over R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]\bigl[\tfrac{1}{[n]_q} : n \ge 1\bigr]

  \log_q(1 + x) \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{(-1)^{n-1}  x^n}{[n]_q}

is primitive (verified by \Delta_q(x^n) and cancellation) and inverse to \exp_q (verified by the q-binomial inversion). Over \mathbb{C} this recovers the convergent series (q-logarithm). Over \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{C}_p existence follows from the corresponding \exp_q existence via the Milnor--Moore adjunction.
prop:q-logarithm-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the q-logarithm primitive (conditional). Conditional on primitive rigidity. Let H be an additive abelian group whose coproduct \Delta_q and counit \epsilon are additive, and suppose primitives are rigid on H: a primitive element with vanishing counit is zero. Then any two q-logarithm primitives sharing \Delta_q and \epsilon coincide.

As for the q-exponential, both hypotheses are steps the accompanying proof already takes — rigidity is its Milnor–Moore assertion that a primitive fixed by D_q with trivial counit vanishes, and additivity is what lets it form \ell_1 - \ell_2. That difference is primitive with vanishing counit, hence zero.

Rigidity is where the content sits, and it is not available here: primitives of a Hopf algebra form a Lie algebra, so they are not in general unique, and it is the grading of \mathcal{H}_q together with the vanishing counit that cuts the relevant space down.
prf:q-logarithm-unique:
Proof Proof of uniqueness of the q-logarithm primitive. Assume the ambient coproduct and counit are additive, and that primitives are rigid: a primitive element with vanishing counit is zero.

The difference \ell_1 - \ell_2 is primitive, since \Delta_q is additive and each \ell_i is primitive; and its counit is 0 - 0 = 0. Rigidity gives \ell_1 - \ell_2 = 0.

Rigidity is the Milnor–Moore shadow of uniqueness of the Lie-algebra logarithm on a connected group, and it is stated as a hypothesis rather than discharged. It cannot be dropped: primitives of a Hopf algebra form a Lie algebra and so are not unique in general, and it is the grading of \mathcal{H}_q together with the vanishing counit that cuts the relevant space down.
sec:q-special-functions-dilog-preamble: This section introduces the q-dilogarithm as the framework's central transcendental object, anchored by its \mathrm{SU}(2) specialisation and Reeb-flow PDE characterisation.
def:q-dilogarithm:
Definition q-Dilogarithm (iterated primitive, categorical). A level-k primitive p_k \in \mathcal{H}_q^{\otimes k} satisfies the shuffle recursion \Delta_q(p_k) = p_k \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes p_k + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} p_i \otimes p_{k-i}. The q-dilogarithm is the unique level-2 primitive \mathrm{Li}_2^q \in \mathcal{H}_q^{\otimes 2} normalised by the pentagon relation

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(y) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q(x) = \mathrm{Li}_2^q(xy) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{x(1-y)}{1-xy}\right) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{y(1-x)}{1-xy}\right).
rem:q-dilogarithm-pentagon-associator:
Remark The q-dilogarithm pentagon as the monoidal associator axiom. The q-dilogarithm is not imported into the framework as a separate datum; it is the solution of a coherence condition the aether category \mathbf{C} already carries. Because \mathbf{C} is monoidal, its associator \alpha_{X,Y,Z}\colon (X\otimes Y)\otimes Z \to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z) satisfies the Mac Lane pentagon coherence — the five reassociations of a fourfold tensor commute. Passing to the shuffle Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q of the braiding, that coherence descends to a functional equation on the level-2 shuffle primitive: the five reassociations collapse to the five-term relation

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(y) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q(x) = \mathrm{Li}_2^q(xy) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{x(1-y)}{1-xy}\right) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{y(1-x)}{1-xy}\right).

By the definition of the q-dilogarithm there is exactly one level-2 primitive satisfying this relation, so the pentagon axiom names \mathrm{Li}_2^q rather than merely constraining it — the dilogarithm is the unique scalar shadow of the associator. In operator form this is the Faddeev–Kashaev identity: the quantum dilogarithm is the quantum associator (equivalently the 6j-symbol), and the operator pentagon

  \Phi(\mathsf P)\,\Phi(\mathsf Q) = \Phi(\mathsf Q)\,\Phi(\mathsf P+\mathsf Q)\,\Phi(\mathsf P)

on a Weyl pair \mathsf P\mathsf Q = \mathsf Q\mathsf P + 1 is the same coherence read as a fusion move.

The equivalence of the pentagon with the q-dilogarithm, proved below, is scalar: a potential on \mathcal{H}_q satisfies the five-term relation exactly when it is a q-dilogarithm datum. The reduction from the morphism-level Mac Lane pentagon on \alpha_{X,Y,Z} to that scalar equation is the classical shuffle--associator identification of Faddeev--Kashaev, and the analytic five-term relation at q \neq 1 remains conjectural. So the pentagon names \mathrm{Li}_2^q within the scalar layer, and the passage from the categorical axiom to that layer rests on the cited identification.

Two faces of the one associator. On the aether branch (real q) the pentagon is realised by the compact dilogarithm \Phi_q / \mathrm{Li}_2^q — the bar-even face that drives mass and binding. Continued to the fibre branch |q|=1, where the compact product's zeros accumulate on the unit circle and it ceases to be well defined, the surviving realisation is Faddeev's non-compact modular double \Phi_b = \Phi_{1/b} (with q = e^{2\pi i b^2}) — the bar-odd face carrying the decay observable. Both solve the same pentagon; they are the two archimedean lenses of the identification of the \Phi_q machinery with the AJ-conjecture machinery in the stochastic-mechanics chapter (real versus root-of-unity saddle of the one \hat{A}_K), not two different objects.

The observable is a pairing, not a product. Where an archimedean number is finally extracted, the dilogarithm associator enters as an analytic operator paired against the algebraic Markov-trace state — a Hopf–Drinfeld pairing (equivalently a q-difference-module action), not a scalar multiplication: the continuous flow is contracted against the finite cyclotomic trace data. This "analytic paired with algebraic" structure fixes the shape of the observable. It does not, by itself, determine the analytic monodromy datum away from the roots of unity — that datum is genuinely resurgent and remains open.

Sources for the operator pentagon and the 6j reading. For complex b in the first quadrant, Faddeev, Kashaev and Volkov prove the five-term identity e_b(\mathsf P)\,e_b(\mathsf X) = e_b(\mathsf X)\,e_b(\mathsf P + \mathsf X)\,e_b(\mathsf P) for self-adjoint \mathsf P, \mathsf X with [\mathsf P, \mathsf X] = 1/(2\pi i), and obtain real b by continuity [faddeev-kashaev-volkov2000, \S6.1, eq. (20), and \S6.5]; with q = e^{i\pi b^2}, complex b in that quadrant gives |q| < 1, and the unitary case |q| = 1 is reached by continuity. Their commutator is normalised by 1/(2\pi i), where the display above uses \mathsf P\mathsf Q = \mathsf Q\mathsf P + 1, so the two agree after rescaling the pair. The identification of the elementary intertwiners attached to diagonal exchanges of ideal triangulations with the Kashaev 6j-symbols is recorded by Baseilhac and Benedetti, who attribute it to earlier work and derive the matrix dilogarithms of the quantum hyperbolic state sums from those 6j-symbols [baseilhac-benedetti-fibred, \S1]. A semiclassical anchor comes from Teschner and Vartanov: as b \to 0, the b-6j symbol of the modular double localises at the two roots u_\pm of dU/du = -2\pi i/u, where U(u,A) is an alternating sum of eight dilogarithms in A_k = e^{i\eta_k}, with exponent W_\pm(A)/(2\pi i b^2), W_\pm(A) = U(u_\pm, A) + \Delta(A) - \tfrac53\pi^2 \mp 2\pi^2\varphi, whose imaginary part is the hyperbolic tetrahedron volume formula they quote from Murakami and Yano [terashima-yamazaki2013, \S\S3.1--3.2, eqs. (3.1)--(3.4) and (3.10)--(3.11)]. Those tetrahedra are non-ideal, fixed by six free dihedral angles, so the anchor does not by itself give \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) or any ideal-triangulation volume; that would need the ideal limit of their eq.~(3.3).
rem:q-dilogarithm-properties: Remark \mathrm{Li}_2^q as the categorical braiding potential (R-matrix). The universal R-matrix of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) admits the compact q-Pochhammer dilogarithm factorisation of Ludwig D. Faddeev and Rinat M. Kashaev [faddeev_kashaev1994] and Ludwig D. Faddeev [faddeev1994], whose logarithm matches the categorical q-dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q at leading order so that \mathrm{Li}_2^q acts as the categorical braiding potential. Under archimedean modular-double realisation, Ludwig D. Faddeev's noncompact integral quantum dilogarithm \Phi_b [faddeev1995] supplies the tetrahedral building block of the three-dimensional state-integral topological quantum field theory constructed by Jørgen Ellegaard Andersen and Rinat M. Kashaev [andersen-kashaev2014] (expounded for the Garoufalidis–Kashaev state-integral invariant by Amelia Palmer Dusenbury [dusenbury2025]).
rem:q-dilog-habiro-ring: Remark Native algebraic home of \mathrm{Li}_2^q: the Habiro ring. The formal series \mathrm{Li}_2^q(x) = \sum_{n \geq 1} x^n / (n\,[n]_q) holds coefficients in the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}[\![x]\!]. Cyclotomic projection evaluates the series at any root of unity without invoking analytic continuation.
rem:q-dilog-three-contexts:
Remark \mathrm{Li}_2^q in \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{C}_p. The extra denominator n forces tighter convergence constraints. Over \mathbb{F}_p, the series truncates to \mathrm{Li}_2^{q,(p)}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{p-1} x^n / (n [n]_q). Over \mathbb{Q}_p and \mathbb{C}_p, it converges within v_p(x) > 1/(p-1).

What the literature covers. The sources treat the undeformed case q = 1. There the finite truncation is the finite polylogarithm \mathrm{li}_n(z) = \sum_{k=1}^{p-1} z^k/k^n, and Besser proves that for \mathrm{Li}^{(p)}_n(z) := \mathrm{Li}_n(z) - \mathrm{Li}_n(z^p)/p^n one has \mathrm{Li}^{(p)}_n(X) \subset W and \mathrm{Li}^{(p)}_n reduces modulo p to (1 - z^p)^{-1}\,\mathrm{li}_n(z), where W is the ring of Witt vectors of \bar{\mathbb{F}}_p and X = \{z \in W : |z| = |z-1| = 1\} [besser2000, §2, Prop. 2.1]; at a root of unity \alpha \in X, p^{-n}\mathrm{Li}_n(\alpha) \equiv -\mathrm{li}_n(\sigma(\alpha))/(1-\alpha) \pmod p [besser2000, Cor. 2.2]. Coleman's p-adic polylogarithms on \mathbb{C}_p are given by the defining power series on the residue disc of 0, and \mathrm{Li}^{(p)}_n is a convergent power series in 1/(1-z) outside \{|z - 1| \le p^{-1/(p-1)}\} [besser-dejeu2008, §2, Thm. 2.7]; that paper gives an algorithm computing them to a prescribed precision [besser-dejeu2008, \S§3--4]. The q-deformed truncation and the threshold v_p(x) > 1/(p-1) stated above are not taken from these sources, which do not treat [n]_q.

On the hopf-algebra tag: algebra closure and the shuffle relation depend on the normalisation. Schlesinger takes \mathrm{Li}_{n_1,\dots,n_m}(z_1,\dots,z_m;q) = \sum_{0<k_1<\dots<k_m} z_1^{k_1}\cdots z_m^{k_m}/\big((1-q^{k_1})^{n_1}\cdots(1-q^{k_m})^{n_m}\big), proves that the rational span of these is an associative \mathbb{Q}-algebra [schlesinger2001, §2, Lemma 2], and derives \mathrm{Li}_1(x;q)\,\mathrm{Li}_1(y;q) = \mathrm{Li}_{1,1}(x,y;q) + \mathrm{Li}_{1,1}(y,x;q) + \mathrm{Li}_2(xy;q) [schlesinger2001, Cor. 3]; the source states that this choice differs from the Kirillov and Koornwinder deformations and is made so that the algebra property holds. Its dilogarithm is \sum_k z^k/(1-q^k)^2, while the one interpreted here is \sum_n x^n/(n[n]_q), so those results are not established for this normalisation by that paper.
rem:q-dilog-archimedean: Remark Archimedean realisation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q (Kirillov dilogarithm). Over \mathbb{C}, the q-dilogarithm represents the convergent Kirillov series \mathrm{Li}_2^q(x) = \sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{x^n}{n [n]_q} for |x| < 1.
rem:q-dilog-heat-partition: Remark \mathrm{Li}_2^q as the q-heat partition function. The q-dilogarithm generates the partition function of the q-heat flow. The contour integral of the resolvent against the spectrum sums logarithmic branches at each eigenvalue \lambda_j(q) to produce \mathrm{Li}_2^q.
rem:q-dilog-physical-meaning: Remark Physical meaning of \mathrm{Li}_2^q: Bethe-ansatz generating function. The q-dilogarithm controls the one-loop correction to the Reeb-flow entropy on the aether.
prop:q-dilogarithm-exists:
Proposition Inhabitation of the q-dilogarithm structure. Over any carrier H with a zero, the q-dilogarithm structure — a level-2 element \mathrm{Li}_2^q, an evaluation map, and the pentagon data — is inhabited.

The statement is inhabitation, not construction. The witness takes the evaluation map identically zero, which satisfies the five-term relation without being the intended solution; producing \mathrm{Li}_2^q itself requires the shuffle recursion over a graded q-shuffle Hopf algebra. Uniqueness is a separate and conditional statement (uniqueness of \mathrm{Li}_2^q, the next proposition), and the zero solution is exactly what its rigidity hypothesis has to exclude.

A zero in H is needed: over a carrier with an addition but no distinguished element the structure can be empty, since it must supply a level-1 primitive \log_q \in H.
prf:q-dilogarithm-exists: Proof Proof of existence of the q-dilogarithm. The shuffle recursion \Delta_q(p_k) = p_k \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes p_k + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} p_i \otimes p_{k-i} with p_0 = 1, p_1 = \log_q has a one-dimensional solution space at each level (up to lower-level primitives). Choosing the normalisation fixed by the pentagon identity uniquely determines \mathrm{Li}_2^q as a specific element at level k = 2. Over \mathbb{C} this recovers the convergent series \sum x^n / (n [n]_q) on |x| < 1. Over \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{C}_p the same shuffle recursion applies with truncation / convergence-radius adjustments as in the (q-dilogarithm) three-context section.
prop:q-dilogarithm-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the q-dilogarithm evaluation (conditional). Conditional on pentagon rigidity. Let H be an additive abelian group carrying the pentagon data (\mathrm{mul}, \mathrm{compl}, \mathrm{div}), and suppose the five-term relation is rigid on H: the only f : H \to H satisfying

f(y) + f(x) = f(xy) + f\!\left(\tfrac{x(1-y)}{1-xy}\right)
  + f\!\left(\tfrac{y(1-x)}{1-xy}\right)

identically is f = 0. Then any two q-dilogarithm structures on H sharing that pentagon data have the same evaluation map, \mathrm{Li}_2^q-eval.

The rigidity hypothesis is the one-dimensionality step of the accompanying proof, carried in the statement rather than assumed silently: the five-term relation is additive in the evaluation map, so the difference of two solutions is again a solution, and rigidity forces it to vanish.

The conclusion is about the evaluation map and not about the level-2 element \mathrm{Li}_2^q itself. That is forced: the pentagon identity constrains the evaluation map only, so no hypothesis on it can determine the element. Determining the element requires a normalisation the present data does not carry.
prf:q-dilogarithm-unique:
Proof Proof of uniqueness of the q-dilogarithm. Assume the five-term relation is rigid on H: the only map satisfying it identically is the zero map.

The relation is additive in the evaluation map, so if two q-dilogarithm structures share the pentagon data (\mathrm{mul}, \mathrm{compl}, \mathrm{div}), the difference of their evaluation maps again satisfies it. Rigidity forces that difference to vanish, so the two evaluation maps agree.

Rigidity is the one-dimensionality of the solution space of the level-2 shuffle recursion modulo lower-level primitives, and it is stated as a hypothesis rather than discharged. The conclusion reaches the evaluation map only: the pentagon identity constrains that map and not the level-2 element \mathrm{Li}_2^q itself, so determining the element needs a normalisation the present data does not carry.
prop:dilog-pentagon-is-associator:
Proposition The pentagon coherence is equivalent to being a q-dilogarithm. Fix the monoidal argument operations — the product x,y \mapsto xy, the complement x \mapsto 1-x, and division. A potential f on the shuffle algebra \mathcal{H}_q satisfies the Mac Lane pentagon (the five-term relation)

  f(y) + f(x) = f(xy) + f\!\left(\frac{x(1-y)}{1-xy}\right) + f\!\left(\frac{y(1-x)}{1-xy}\right)

if and only if it is the evaluation map of a q-dilogarithm datum with those arguments.

The equivalence holds because a q-dilogarithm datum is defined by this pentagon, so it restates that definition. It does not show that the rigid-monoidal axioms of \mathbf{C} force \mathrm{Li}_2^q; that requires the categorical-to-scalar reduction stated in the scope boundary below. Together with the uniqueness of the level-2 primitive (inhabitation of the q-dilogarithm structure), the pentagon axiom names \mathrm{Li}_2^q.

Two guises of the one pentagon

The same Mac Lane coherence has already appeared above in two guises, which this proposition records as one law:

  • Cochain / 3-cocycle guise. The additive twist associator \alpha = dF satisfies the pentagon automatically because d^2 = 0.
  • Dilogarithm five-term guise. The pentagon condition of the q-dilogarithm datum, whose operator form is the Faddeev–Kashaev pentagon \Phi(\mathsf P)\Phi(\mathsf Q) = \Phi(\mathsf Q)\Phi(\mathsf P+\mathsf Q)\Phi(\mathsf P) (the q-dilogarithm pentagon as the monoidal associator axiom).

A third, braided guise is in the literature at a root of unity. McPhail-Snyder and Reshetikhin show that the holonomy braiding of U_\xi(\mathfrak{sl}_2) at a positive, non-pinched, log-colored crossing factors as \tfrac1N Z_b(Z_r \otimes Z_l) Z_t, each factor defined by a quantum dilogarithm [mcphail-snyder-reshetikhin2025, §4.3, Thm. 4.5, eq. (4.19)], and that these R-matrices satisfy a holonomy Yang--Baxter equation for admissible colorings [mcphail-snyder-reshetikhin2025, §4.4, Thm. 4.7]. That is a statement about the braiding at a root of unity; it does not supply the scalar equivalence of this proposition or the categorical-to-scalar reduction of the scope boundary below.

Proof outline

The biconditional holds over an arbitrary carrier with an addition, with no further structure. The forward direction packages the solution of the pentagon as a q-dilogarithm datum; the reverse reads the datum's five-term condition.

Scope boundary

The equivalence is at the level of the scalar pentagon potential. The categorical \to scalar reduction (that the morphism-level Mac Lane pentagon on \alpha_{X,Y,Z} reduces to this scalar five-term equation) is the classical shuffle–associator identification of Faddeev–Kashaev; the analytic five-term relation at q \neq 1 remains conjectural.
rem:generating-functions-solve-reeb-flow:
Remark Generating functions (\exp_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q, categorical Fourier) are the Reeb-flow solutions. The functions \exp_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q, and the categorical Fourier transform constitute the exact algebraic solutions to the characteristic flow equations on the Reeb bundle within the Habiro completion.

  1. \exp_q provides the formal solution of the base Reeb-flow equation L_{\xi_q} Z = J\hbar_q Z.
  2. The categorical Fourier transform diagonalises the q-heat equation \partial_t u = -\Delta_q u across Peter–Weyl isotypic components.
  3. \mathrm{Li}_2^q evaluates the volumetric expansion of the Reeb-heat flow. Under the archimedean realisation \tau_\infty, it produces the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm.

These three functions are the unique algebraic objects in the Habiro completion satisfying the categorical evolution equations.
prop:pre-archimedean-figure-eight-bloch-:
Proposition The figure-eight Nahm equation gives a class in the Bloch group of \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}). Proposition. Let F be a field. Write \mathcal{P}(F) for the pre-Bloch group: the free abelian group on symbols [z], z \in F \setminus \{0,1\}, modulo the five-term relations

  [x] - [y] + \Bigl[\frac{y}{x}\Bigr] - \Bigl[\frac{1-x^{-1}}{1-y^{-1}}\Bigr] + \Bigl[\frac{1-x}{1-y}\Bigr] = 0 .

Write \mathcal{B}(F) = \ker\bigl(\delta \colon \mathcal{P}(F) \to \textstyle\bigwedge^2_{\mathbb{Z}} F^\times\bigr) with \delta[z] = z \wedge (1-z). Let

  T_m(q) \;=\; \prod_{j=1}^{m} (1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j})

be the m-th summand of the figure-eight Habiro series. Then:

  1. T_{m+1} = T_m \cdot (1-qX)(1-q^{-1}X^{-1}) with X = q^m, so the Nahm equation of the summand is (1-X)(1-X^{-1}) = 1.
  2. For X \neq 0, the Nahm equation holds if and only if X^2 - X + 1 = 0.
  3. Every solution X \in F gives [X] \in \mathcal{B}(F), and \delta[X] = 0 already in \bigwedge^2 F^\times.
  4. For F = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6) = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}), the class 2[\zeta_6] lies in \mathcal{B}(F).

Proof. Item 1 is the last factor of the product. For item 2, multiply the Nahm equation by X. For item 3, X^2 - X + 1 = 0 gives 1 - X = X^{-1}, so \delta[X] = X \wedge X^{-1} = -(X \wedge X) = 0. Item 4 is item 3 at the primitive sixth root of unity, which satisfies \zeta_6^2 - \zeta_6 + 1 = 0. \square

Every statement is algebraic over F; no limit, integral or numerical value enters. The archimedean step is separate. The Bloch–Wigner function D is a homomorphism \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}, and D(e^{i\pi/3}) = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{Vol}(4_1). That evaluation is the figure-eight case of archimedean realisation compatibility, not of this proposition. The identification of 2[\zeta_6] with the class of the hyperbolic structure on the figure-eight complement is the standard computation from its two regular ideal tetrahedra [zagier-dilogarithm]; it is cited here, not proved. The scope is the figure-eight knot only.
conj:archimedean-realisation-volume-comp:
Conjecture Compatibility of the local archimedean realisation \tau_\infty with the global realization \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} on QOU volume classes. The local archimedean realisation functor \tau_\infty \colon \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{C}[\![q-1]\!] acts on the Habiro-ring volume. The global archimedean realization functor \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} \colon \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \to \mathbb{R} evaluates the motivic volume class.

Conjecturally, for every QOU braid \beta, the archimedean value of the Habiro-ring volume and the topological realization of the motivic volume coincide with the hyperbolic volume:

  \mathrm{ev}_{q \to 1}\bigl(\tau_\infty(-\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V_0(\beta)))\bigr) = \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}\bigl(\mu(\beta)\bigr) = V_{\mathrm{hyp}}(K_\beta).

For the figure-eight knot the conjecture factors in two steps. The first is algebraic and proved: the Nahm equation of the Habiro summand gives the class 2[\zeta_6] in the Bloch group of \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) (pre-Archimedean figure-eight class). The second is the archimedean regulator: \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2D(e^{i\pi/3}).
sec:braiding-conventions-intro: This section consolidates the sign and orientation conventions binding the aether parameter q, the imaginary unit i, and the ribbon twist v = q^{1/2}.
rem:braiding-unit-circle-convention: Remark The unit-circle convention for the braiding eigenvalue. The inside-unit-circle convention assigns q := \lambda_+, where \lambda_+ is the eigenvalue of c_{V,V} on the symmetric summand S^2 V. For real q > 1, \lambda_+ = q lies outside the unit circle and \lambda_- = -q^{-1} lies inside. This convention secures positivity for the symmetric eigenvalue and aligns with the standard orientation of the Kauffman bracket.
rem:sqrt-q-ribbon-structure: Remark The element \sqrt{q} and the ribbon structure. The element v := q^{1/2} constitutes post-Archimedean naming. A ribbon structure on \mathbf{C} demands a natural twist \varTheta_V \colon V \xrightarrow{\sim} V. On the defining \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation, the twist axiom forces \varTheta_V = q^{1/2}\mathrm{id}_V. The binary sign choice on v dictates the spin structure on the realized worldline.
rem:sign-as-spin-structure: Remark The sign of \sqrt{q} as a spin structure. The relation v^2 = q specifies v = q^{1/2} up to sign. Post-archimedean, this binary sign determines the spin structure on the realized worldline.
rem:i-as-braiding-orientation:
Remark The imaginary unit i as braiding-orientation datum. The imaginary unit i serves as the orientation of the braiding c_{V,V} versus c_{V,V}^{-1}.

  1. Wick rotation: The rotation t \mapsto it converting the Laplace half-plane to the Fourier half-plane flips upon i \mapsto -i.
  2. CR complex structure: The operator J \colon H \to H secures the CR orientation.
  3. Arrow of time: The positive crossing c_{V,V} defines forward time in the Hecke basis ordering, while c_{V,V}^{-1} reverses it. Negating i equates to flipping the crossing orientation.
rem:affine-chart-origin-of-i-and-q:
Remark Affine-chart origin of the categorical coordinates i and q. Both categorical coordinates of \mathbb{P}(V) originate from the transition between the Reeb chart U_0 and the antipodal chart U_1, governed by z \cdot w = \kappa.

For \mathbb{P}_q(V), the homogeneous coordinates satisfy the quantum-plane relation yx = q\,xy. The charts are z = y x^{-1} and w = y^{-1} x, yielding z w = q^{-1}. The aether parameter q acts precisely as the chart-transition coefficient. The ordering of each quotient matters: the pair z = y x^{-1}, w = x y^{-1} multiplies to 1 in any ring, so the coefficient q^{-1} comes from the relation yx = q\,xy and not from the affine charts alone.

At q = 1, the transition degenerates to z w = 1. The chart-swap involution \iota(z) = z^{-1} generates a \mathbb{Z}_2 automorphism. The quarter-turn generator \rho_{\pi/2} = i \mathrm{id}_V operates as the square root of \iota, identifying i as the categorical coordinate. The Galois action exchanging \pm i encapsulates the braiding orientation choice c_{V,V} \leftrightarrow c_{V,V}^{-1}.
prop:reeb-u1-chart-swap:
Proposition Chart-swap U(1) equals the Reeb U(1) as subgroups of \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}(V)). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. As subgroups of \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbb{P}(V)):

  \langle \rho_{\theta_q} : \theta_q \in U(1) \rangle = \langle \phi_t : t \in \mathbb{R} \rangle = T_q.

The chart-swap one-parameter subgroup and the Reeb flow subgroup coincide as the image of the maximal torus T_q.
prf:reeb-u1-chart-swap:
Proof Proof of reeb u1 chart swap. The argument is the routine identification "T_q-orbits on the projective quotient are unique up to reparameterisation".

Step 1: T_q acts canonically on \mathbb{P}(V). The projective-line object \mathbb{P}(V) = G_q / T_q is, by construction, the quotient of G_q by the right action of T_q. The residual left T_q-action on G_q descends to a well-defined T_q-action on the quotient, yielding a canonical homomorphism T_q \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbb{P}(V)). The image is a one-dimensional connected subgroup, hence a U(1).

Step 2: the Reeb flow factors through this T_q. By construction (Constructive Reeb derivation on Bring's coordinate ring), the Reeb generator \xi = e_3 \in \mathfrak{su}(2) is the infinitesimal generator of the maximal torus T_q \subset G_q. The one-parameter group \phi_t = \exp(t \xi) \subset G_q is therefore exactly T_q (as a real one-parameter group). Its induced action on \mathbb{P}(V) = G_q / T_q is the standard T_q-action of Step 1. Hence \langle \phi_t \rangle = T_q \subset \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbb{P}(V)).

Step 3: the chart-swap factors through the same T_q. By affine-chart origin of i and q, the chart-swap family \rho_\varTheta : Z \mapsto e^{i\varTheta} Z on the affine coordinate Z of the contact affine chart is the U(1) acting on \mathbb{P}(V) by scaling the standard affine chart at 0. This scaling is, by construction of the projective quotient \mathbb{P}(V) = G_q / T_q, the induced left T_q-action of Step 1 (the T_q-grading on the affine coordinate Z has weight -1 for Z = y x^{-1}, hence T_q scales Z by a phase). Hence \langle \rho_\varTheta \rangle = T_q \subset \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbb{P}(V)).

Step 4: conclusion. Both subgroups equal T_q by Steps 2–3, so they are equal as subgroups of \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbb{P}(V)). \square

Explicit parameterisation (corollary). The two parameterisations differ only by a scale and sign determined by SU(2) conventions. With \xi = e_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{diag}(1, -1) and Z = y x^{-1} (x weight +\tfrac{1}{2}, y weight -\tfrac{1}{2}, so Z has T_q-weight -1), the flow acts as

  \phi_t \cdot Z  =  e^{-t}\, Z  =  \rho_{i t}(Z)
  \qquad (\text{equivalently } \varTheta = i\,t),

consequently the chart-swap parameter \varTheta and the Reeb parameter t are related by Wick rotation \varTheta = i\,t (real Reeb time \leftrightarrow imaginary chart-swap angle, recovering the Bargmann–Hall–Wightman forward-tube reading).
rem:reeb-u1-five-roles:
Remark Five roles of the Reeb U(1): Wick rotation, i, chart-swap, knot framing, OS reflection. The maximal torus T_q of the aether G_q plays five distinct roles:

  1. Antipodal involution: \rho_\pi : Z \mapsto -Z (\mathbb{Z}_2 at \theta_q = \pi).
  2. Imaginary unit i: \rho_{\pi/2} (\mathbb{Z}_4).
  3. Wick rotation: \rho_{\theta_q} (full U(1)).
  4. Reeb flow \phi_t: Z \mapsto e^{-t} Z (generated by \xi).
  5. q-deformation: \rho_{\theta_q} off the unit circle (U_q(1)).

The continuous Wick rotation is the analytic continuation of the Reeb-flow parameter. Knot operators function as Reeb-U(1) Wilson loops on the contact bundle. The Osterwalder-Schrader reflection embodies the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 \subset T_q subgroup.
prop:categorical-coordinate-ring:
Proposition The categorical-coordinate ring R[i, q^{\pm 1}] of chart-transition data on \mathbb{P}_q(V). Let R be the categorical ground ring and \mathbb{P}(V) the projective line object. The categorical-coordinate ring of the chart-transition data of the deformation family (\mathbb{P}_q(V))_{q \in R^\times} is

  R[i, q^{\pm 1}] = R[q, q^{-1}][i] / (i^2 + 1).

It acts as the smallest R-algebra extension wherein the chart-transition coefficient q^{-1} is a unit and the tangent representation \rho_p(\iota) = -1 admits a square root. The chart-transition automorphism group factors as the semidirect product

  \mathrm{Aut}_{R[i, q^{\pm 1}]}(U_0 \cap U_1, \mathbb{P}_q(V)) \cong \langle q \rangle \rtimes \langle \iota \rangle.
prf:categorical-coordinate-ring:
Proof Proof of categorical coordinate ring. Existence: S = R[q, q^{-1}][i]/(i^2+1) visibly satisfies (1) by construction of the Laurent polynomial ring and (2) via i = image of the polynomial generator. The semidirect-product factorisation follows from \iota \cdot z \cdot \iota^{-1} = z^{-1} on \mathbb{G}_m, which transports through the quantum-plane relation y x = q\, x y to give \iota \cdot q \cdot \iota^{-1} = q^{-1} on the chart-transition coefficient.

Semidirect, not direct. Composing the three maps in the chart-transition group on the affine coordinate z:

  z  \;\xrightarrow{\iota^{-1}}\;  z^{-1}
   \;\xrightarrow{q\,\cdot}\;  q z^{-1}
   \;\xrightarrow{\iota}\;  (q z^{-1})^{-1}
   \;=\;  q^{-1} z,

so \iota \cdot q \cdot \iota^{-1} = q^{-1}. The chart-swap inverts the scaling parameter — a non-trivial \mathbb{Z}_2 action on \langle q \rangle — forcing the semidirect (not direct) product. Equivalent reading: q and q^{-1} are the two eigenvalues of the braiding (\lambda_+ = q, \lambda_- = -q^{-1}), and the chart-swap is exactly the involution exchanging them (rem:braiding-unit-circle-convention).

The same semidirect persists in the commutative limit: in R[i, q^{\pm 1}] the chart-swap acts on the i-generator by

  \iota \cdot i \cdot \iota^{-1}  \;=\;  -i,

since the Galois action \mathrm{Gal}(R[i]/R) = \mathbb{Z}_2 on \pm i coincides with the chart-swap \mathbb{Z}_2 (one \mathbb{Z}_2, three faces — chart-swap, Galois, braiding orientation — per rem:i-as-braiding-orientation).

Universality: any R-algebra S satisfying (1) and (2) admits a unique R-algebra homomorphism R[q, q^{-1}] \to S sending the Laurent generator to the chosen q \in S^\times (universal property of Laurent polynomials), and a unique extension to R[q, q^{-1}][i]/(i^2 + 1) \to S sending i to the chosen square root (universal property of polynomial-ring quotients).

The two structural pieces — invertible scaling generator and square root of involution-eigenvalue — are exactly the data recorded by the affine-chart-origin remark (rem:affine-chart-origin-of-i-and-q). \square

Specialisations.

Specialisation Resulting ring Interpretation
q \mapsto 1, R = \mathbb{C} \mathbb{C} (as i \in \mathbb{C}) Archimedean commutative limit
q \mapsto 1, R = \mathbb{R} \mathbb{C} = \mathbb{R}[i] Smallest archimedean ring with i
q \mapsto e^{2\pi i/N}, R = \mathbb{C} \mathbb{C} Root-of-unity (anyonic) limit
Universal R = \mathbb{Z} \mathbb{Z}[i, q, q^{-1}] Lusztig integral form with i

Relation to existing structure. The proposition is a structural statement: it does not add new categorical content beyond (rem:affine-chart-origin-of-i-and-q) but pins down the universal R-algebra extension that makes the informal categorical-coordinate principle precise. The convention q := \lambda_+ (rem:braiding-unit-circle-convention) fixes which Laurent generator is named q; the sign of i is fixed by the braiding orientation (rem:i-as-braiding-orientation).
sec:elaboration-intro: The remaining sections elaborate the categorical, algebraic, and analytic context of the QOU axioms. They establish the TQFT setting, record the q-jacobiator identity, give the physical reading of the categorical action, and assemble the categorical lifting for the brane tower.
rem:tqft-context:
Remark TQFT context. The axioms of the quantum universe and quantum observable universe are modelled on the algebraic data of topological quantum field theory. The Frobenius--Hopf object A carries the 2d cobordism data and the Hopf structure for quantum-group symmetry. The precise form of the 2d-cobordism claim is the canonical isomorphism \mathbf{Cob}(2) \cong \mathbf{Cob}(3)_{S^2,\mathrm{CF}} [li2026-two-sphere] (Thm.~1.0.8): the commutative-Frobenius part of the S^2-sector of the oriented 3d bordism category is the 2d cobordism category, so Z(S^2) is a commutative Frobenius monoid for every 3d TFT Z, and its Frobenius structure is exactly the 2d cobordism data. The sector's remaining generators, one unit per closed oriented irreducible prime 3-manifold (Thm.~1.0.5), are not used by these axioms. The identification is at the level of the Frobenius structure only: Li's monoids are commutative in a symmetric monoidal target, whereas A is a Hopf algebra in a braided category and is not assumed commutative, and nothing here identifies A with Z(S^2) of a 3d TFT or bears on the Hopf half of the Frobenius--Hopf object.

The condition \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 acts as the categorical contact condition. It is the condition that would ensure irreducibility of an associated 3d TQFT; no such TQFT is constructed here, and at generic q > 1 the representation category has infinitely many simple objects, so it is not modular (unlike the compact-Lie-group extended 3d TQFTs classified by Daniel S. Freed, Michael J. Hopkins, Jacob Lurie, and Constantin Teleman [freed2010]). Within the framework it ensures non-degeneracy of the pairing across cobordisms, and full dualisability. In the archimedean realisation, this enforces H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0, eliminating infinitesimal automorphisms on the instanton connection.
